card.title: Newton's first law
card.body: If $\sum \vec{F} = \vec{0}$, an object stays at rest or keeps moving at **constant velocity** (same speed, same direction).
card.says: you do not need a net force to keep moving; you only need one to **change** velocity.
card.from: Galileo's thought experiments on frictionless ramps and Isaac Newton's *Principia* (1687), also called the **law of inertia**.
card.useWhen: an object is stationary or moving steadily in a straight line, so every pair of opposing force components must cancel ($\sum \vec{F} = \vec{0}$).
card.example: A 1,200 kg car cruises straight at a constant $20\text{ m/s}$ with a $450\text{ N}$ forward driving force → $\sum F = 0$, so total drag and rolling resistance is $450\text{ N}$ backward.
card.analogy: Standing on a bus when it brakes hard: your feet stop with the floor, while your upper body keeps moving forward.
